I am an old man now, 78 years, and I have farmed in Iringa all my life. This small plot near the house, only a small piece, I plant maize together with beans as I have always done — the beans help the soil and feed the family. I cannot afford the chemical fertilizer from the shop, it is too expensive and the price keeps rising, so I use the manure from my few animals and the kitchen ash. My sons and their wives help me with the digging and weeding because my back is not strong like before, and for the harvest time I may pay one or two young men from the village to help carry.
